newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Some Telstra concerns met - Australian senator.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Some Telstra concerns met - Australian senator.

text.p: Key Australian Independent senator Brian Harradine said on Thursday the government had met some of his concerns about the partial sale of telecoms carrier Telstra Corp.
The upper house of parliament, the Senate, is expected to hold a final vote on the sale plan later on Thursday.

Its fate lies with Harradine and fellow Independent Mal Colston as the only possible sources of the two extra votes the government needs to pass any legislation in the non-government dominated Senate.
"I will be listening most carefully to what (Communications Minister) Senator (Richard) Alston is going to say," Harradine told reporters.
"On the matters of employment and on the matters of the recognition of Tasmania's pre-eminent position in the natural heritage, that implies that those matters have gone reasonably well."
But Harradine said he remained concerned about the method of the Telstra sale.

Australian Treasurer Peter Costello rejected on Tuesday Harradine's proposal that Telstra should be sold through redeemable preference shares, saying the financial markets would be unable to cope with such an issue.
"That's a matter which you'll just have to wait and see as to what Senator Alston might or might not say," Harradine said.
The government plans to raise about A$8.0 billion through the sale of one-third of Telstra with A$1.0 billion of the proceeds earmarked for an environment package.
